I am examining how frontend API requests authenticate.

The frontend auth interceptor lives in `web/src/connect.ts`. It manages an access token stored in localStorage and a refresh token sent as an HTTP-only cookie. The backend package that validates these tokens is `server/auth`, with the Connect authorizer delegating to `auth.Authenticator` in `server/router/api/v1/authz.go`.

The frontend auth interceptor lives at `web/src/connect.ts`. It manages an access token sent as a Bearer header and coordinates refresh via a refresh token cookie.

Backend validation happens through `server/auth`'s `Authenticator`, used via `Authorizer` in the API v1 layer. The frontend does not use PATs for normal browser sessions.
